fields.statement: At 302d9b36, built rhiza and in a scratch repo made a landed change set and a draft each with a recorded open question blocking a node they touch: rhiza inbox printed Nothing waits on you. Then an accepted change set touching store with store-q blocking store: rhiza inbox showed a blocker item (question: Which store? (store-q), blocks: store, change set Accepted) and --json kind blocker with handle/blocks/question. Adding a run-log question on the same change set and a proposed change set blocked directly by cs-q listed the run question, the store-q blocker, and a blocks: this change set blocker together. After answering store-q the blocker was gone (Nothing waits on you).

At 302d9b36, with the built binary in a scratch repo: rhiza question answer store-q "use sqlite" --change <accepted cs> --dry-run --json reported dry_run true and ready still listed store-q; an unknown question and a blank answer each exit 2 with code usage; answering a capability exits 2 (not a question); the real answer wrote decision answer-store-q (statement and quote use sqlite, quote_where the owner, answering question store-q, answers store-q) and ready no longer lists the blocker; a second answer got answer-store-q-2. In the real roadmap app (rhiza tui app roadmap in a pty), enter on the change set, enter on the blocking question, typing use postgres and enter showed Recorded your answer to store-q, Blocking questions none, and the Decision answer-store-q was in the blocked change set.

At 302d9b36, drove the real inbox app (rhiza tui app inbox in a pty) on a scratch repo whose current change set was a draft and where store-q blocks an accepted change set: a opened the answer prompt on the blocker item, typing use sqlite then enter showed answer done and Nothing waits on you; rhiza show answer-store-q --change <accepted cs> showed the Decision quoting use sqlite, linked answers store-q, in the blocked change set rather than the current draft. In a copy, a, typing, then esc and r left the blocker listed and wrote no decision. The run-question session.message path needs a live Rex session and was covered only by the Go fake-runner test.
